Earth is rapidly changing changing, affecting the lives of everyone, including our students.
Reflecting these changes in the environment, interest is growing in the science of water and climate.
Our proposal addresses the need for a new option focused on these two important topics.
Therefore, the goal is to establish Water and Climate Sciences as an option under the existing major in Geology and Geological Oceanography - BS.

Further, an increasing need to analyze large datasets will require our students to obtain higher-level data skills for competing in the workforce.

As the interests and career opportunities for our students have become more diverse, we are seeking to allow more flexibility in selecting professional electives most appropriate for each individual.
The best preparation for many students is something in between our existing Pre-Professional Exercise Science and Applied Exercise Science specializations.
Additionally, it is currently difficult for students who begin in the Pre-Professional Exercise Science specialization and then realize it is not the best fit to change to the Applied Exercise Science specialization without impeding progress toward graduation.
This proposal combines the Professional Content Area courses from each of those specializations into a single list of Professional Electives students can select from.
It will replace the existing Pre-Professional and Applied Exercise Science specialization options in the catalog, but in practice will allow students to choose Professional Electives aligning with either of those specializations or a combination of the two.

The Kinesiology program is currently accredited by the Committee on Accreditation for the Exercise Sciences and this proposal will not change anything associated with that accreditation.
This specialization continues to provide opportunities for students to participate in the department's active research program and community engagement opportunities through active learning courses and internships in alignment with the University's Mission.
It provides the basic science and core kinesiology content area background as well as professional elective options necessary to prepare students for careers that have a great impact on social, cultural, and economic ecosystems in RI and beyond (Strategic Plan Goal 1) including many in healthcare.
The specialization allows students opportunities for study abroad and international internship experiences such as the TEAN program placing our majors in internships in Australia (Strategic Plan Goal 2 Action 3).
Students will also be able to gain hands on research experience working with faculty throughout the department (Strategic Plan Goal 3).

The only specializations this overlaps with are our department's current specializations of Pre-Professional Exercise Science and Applied Exercise Science.
This proposal will replace both of those with this single Kinesiology specialization, so there will be no lasting conflicts or overlaps.
Students currently in the Pre-Professional Exercise Science and Applied Exercise Science specializations will be able to complete the programs they have already started, and incoming students will be entered into the new Kinesiology specialization.

1.10.20 Background. The University of Rhode Island, the state’s land and sea grant research institution began as the state of Rhode Island’s Agricultural Experiment Station and agricultural school chartered in 1888. In 1892, the institution’s name was changed to the Rhode Island College of Agriculture and the Mechanic Arts. This name was subsequently changed to Rhode Island State College in 1909. The current name- the University of Rhode Island— was adopted in 1951 by an act of the State of Rhode Island’s General Assembly. For a complete history of the University, refer to https://www.uri.edu/about/history/ . Administrative Report July, 2024

1.10.30 Mission. The University of Rhode Island is the state’s flagship land and sea grant research institution, with a commitment to urban initiatives. A student-centered research institution, URI actively partners with other organizations globally and locally to advance knowledge and to develop informed residents and leaders. URI is committed to high-quality education, community engagement, and solving the world’s most important challenges. Situated on the traditional land and territories of the Narragansett Nation and the Niantic People, URI strives to create a diverse and inclusive environment for researchers, teachers, learners, and community members. 1.20.11 Composition of the Board Trustees and Quorum Requirements .
Initial membership of the Board of Trustees is defined in the original R.I. Gen. Laws §16 – 32 – 2.2.
The Board of Trustees shall consist of seventeen (17) voting members and five (5) non-voting ex officio members, including:

The President of the University of Rhode Island will appoint one (1) faculty member and one (1) student member who shall be a full-time student in good standing at the University, and who shall both serve in non-voting, ex officio capacity for a single two (2) year term.

Teaching, Advising, and Assessment Committee Report #2024-2025-01 May 1, 2025 Faculty Senate Meeting Amends the University Manual: Appendix C, Sections 4.30-4.34.
RATIONALE During Academic Year 2023-2024, the University created a new permanent committee known as JAPROA (The Joint Committee on Academic Program Review and Outcomes Assessment, per Faculty Senate Bill #23-24-8).
The Committee essentially merged the activities of two former standing committees, the Academic Program Review Committee (APRC) and the Learning Outcomes Oversight Committee (LOOC).
Given the new Committee’s inclusion of Assessment in its charge, the Teaching, Advising, and Assessment Committee’s (TAAC) charge seems ripe for revision to reduce overlap and eliminate any confusion or lack of clarity concerning committee scope and authority.
Around the same time, FSEC had separately taken note that no standing committee at the university is assigned to review admissions and retention data and advise the administration regarding admissions.
Adoption of the proposed language would incorporate university admissions into the charge of the TAAC.

EXISTING LANGUAGE 4.30 The Teaching, Advising, and Assessment Committee shall comprise five or more faculty members, and consider and make recommendations to the Faculty Senate on the items specifically assigned to it (see By-laws 4.31-4.34).
The Committee shall study and make recommendations to the Faculty Senate (or return the matters unapproved, with comments, to the units from which they originated) on the following matters referred to it by the various colleges, schools, the Faculty Senate or its Executive Committee, the Administration, or from another authoritative source, or taken up by the Committee on its own initiative: #21-22-37 4.31 The Committee shall promote good teaching, advising, and assessment at the University by conducting and reporting to the Faculty Senate an annual audit of programs, activities, policies, etc., which are available at the University to support good teaching and assessment and undertake each year, in cooperation with other interested parties, an initiative designed to improve teaching and assessment practices at the University.

Chapter 11 – University Manual

11.10.10 Changes to the University Manual may be made through legislative action of the Faculty Senate and in accordance with the Constitution and By-laws of the Faculty Senate. Final action by the Senate on a proposal to change the Manual shall not be taken unless the proposal appears on the agenda for the meeting. A proposal which appears on the agenda may be amended from the floor and final action on the amended version may be taken at that meeting. Proposed changes to the University Manual deemed editorial by the Constitution, By-Laws and University Manual Committee will be provided as a report to the Faculty Senate and will require
no action. Following the report, any Faculty Senator may move that a proposed change should be considered substantive. This motion, when seconded, will then be considered for a vote, and if passed, the matter shall be handled as a substantive change and will follow University Manual legislative procedures. #13-14–13 #21-22-10
11.10.11 Changes to the University Manual may also be made by the President in those areas corresponding to presidential responsibility and authority. #13-14–13, #21-22-6

11.10.12 The Coordinator, Faculty Senate, shall be the editor of the University Manual; shall assist the Constitution, By-laws, and University Manual Committee with properly incorporating all changes; maintain an accurate current electronic copy of the University Manual on the Faculty Senate website; and maintain, on the Faculty Senate website, a page or pages with superseded University Manual, constitution, and by-laws sections, with indications when and how they were superseded. #00-01–30 , #13-14–13
11.10.13 University Manual changes based on Faculty Senate action. Following necessary approval of Senate action, University Manual changes shall be submitted to the Chair of the Constitution, By-Laws and University Manual Committee for editorial review, to ensure that they are consistent with the style, format, and arrangement of the University Manual (By-laws of the Faculty Senate, Section 4.25 ). Following that review, the Coordinator, Faculty Senate, shall incorporate them into the electronic copy of the University Manual. #13-14–13
